This marks a significant step for off-the-shelf cell therapies targeting cancer and transplantation medicine.

canonical_title: Myanmar Earthquake: 5.2M Tremor Near Yangon Shakes Southeast Asia
summary: A 5.2 magnitude earthquake struck southern Myanmar on May 18, 2026, at a depth of 10 km, with the epicenter 35 km southeast of Yangon. Up to 42,000 people were exposed to strong shaking and 238,000 to moderate shaking. Tremors were also felt in Thailand, including Bangkok, Lampang, and Chiang Mai. Buildings were evacuated as a precaution, though no casualties were immediately reported.

canonical_title: Hantavirus Outbreak on Cruise Ship MV Hondius Raises Pandemic Concerns
summary: As of May 8, 2026, a hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulted in eight reported cases and three deaths, according to the WHO. Spain began evacuating passengers near Tenerife. Analysts warned that a broader health crisis in the current economic climate — with US inflation at 3.3% and stretched policy room — could trigger volatile reactions across global markets, drawing comparisons to the early days of COVID-19.

canonical_title: New Graphene Breakthrough Supercharges Energy Storage
summary: Engineers at Monash University developed a new graphene architecture called multiscale reduced graphene oxide (M-rGO) that achieves record energy and power densities in supercapacitors, potentially rivaling traditional batteries while enabling dramatically faster charging for EVs and electronics.

canonical_title: MIT Physicists Observe Key Evidence of Unconventional Superconductivity in Magic-Angle Graphene
summary: MIT physicists reported the most direct evidence to date of unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted tri-layer graphene (MATTG), finding a distinct V-shaped superconducting gap that suggests electron pairing driven by strong electronic interactions rather than lattice vibrations — a crucial step toward room-temperature superconductors.
